Title: Package Declaration
Code: package main
Explain: Every Go file starts with a package declaration.

Title: Variable Declaration
Code:
var name string = "hello"
var count int = 42
Explain: Declare typed variables with var keyword and initial values.

Title: Short Variable Declaration
Explain: Short declaration infers the type from the right-hand side.

Title: Constant Declaration
Code:
const Pi = 3.14159
const MaxRetries = 5
Explain: Constants are immutable values known at compile time.

Title: Import Statement
Explain: Grouped imports use parentheses to list multiple packages.

Title: Multiple Assignment
Code:
a, b := 1, 2
a, b = b, a
Explain: Go supports multiple assignment and easy value swapping.

Title: Hello World Function
Explain: The main function is the entry point of a Go program.
fmt.Println writes to standard output with a newline.

Title: Simple If-Else
Explain: If-else chains test conditions in order.
The final return acts as the default case.

Title: Basic For Loop
Explain: Go has only one loop keyword: for.
The three-component form mirrors C-style for loops.

Title: Function With Multiple Returns
Explain: Go functions can return multiple values.
Returning an error as the last value is idiomatic Go.

Title: Switch Statement
Explain: Switch cases in Go do not fall through by default.
Multiple values can share a single case.

Title: Slice Filter
Explain: Higher-order functions accept other functions as parameters.
append grows a slice dynamically.
range iterates over slices returning index and value.

Title: Read File Lines
Explain: defer ensures the file is closed when the function exits.
bufio.Scanner reads input line by line.
Errors are propagated up to the caller.

Title: Map Word Count
Explain: make initializes a map ready for use.
strings.Fields splits on whitespace.
Map values default to zero, so ++ works on first access.

Title: Fibonacci With Loop
Explain: make with a length pre-allocates the slice.
Guard clauses handle edge cases early.
Iterative approach avoids recursion overhead.

Title: Error Wrapping
Explain: The %w verb wraps errors preserving the original for errors.Is/As.
Each failure point adds context before returning.
json.Unmarshal decodes JSON into a struct pointer.

Title: Struct With Methods
Explain: Pointer receivers allow methods to mutate the struct.
Pop returns a bool to indicate success without panicking.
Slice reslicing with [:n] removes the last element efficiently.

Title: Sorted Insert
Explain: sort.SearchInts performs binary search on a sorted slice.
copy shifts elements right to make room for insertion.
Merge uses two pointers to combine sorted slices in O(n).

Title: JSON Struct Tags
Explain: Struct tags control JSON field names during marshal/unmarshal.
Validation after parsing catches missing required fields.
Error messages include the index for easier debugging.

Title: String Builder
Explain: strings.Builder avoids repeated allocations from string concat.
Grow pre-allocates buffer capacity when the size is known.
Separators are added before elements starting from the second.

Title: Custom Sort Interface
Explain: The sort.Interface requires Len, Less, and Swap methods.
sort.Reverse wraps an interface to invert the ordering.
Copying before sorting preserves the original slice.

Title: Interface Polymorphism
Explain: Interfaces define behavior contracts without implementation.
Types satisfy interfaces implicitly by implementing all methods.
A slice of interfaces can hold any conforming concrete type.

Title: Goroutine Fan-Out
Explain: WaitGroup coordinates completion of multiple goroutines.
Each goroutine writes to its own index avoiding data races.
defer wg.Done ensures the counter decrements even on early return.

Title: Channel Pipeline
Explain: Directional channel types enforce send-only or receive-only.
Closing a channel signals no more values will be sent.
Pipelines compose stages where each reads from the previous.

Title: Context Timeout
Explain: context.WithTimeout cancels the request after the deadline.
defer cancel releases resources even if the request completes early.
NewRequestWithContext binds the context to the HTTP lifecycle.

Title: Generic Map Function
Explain: Type parameters with any constraint accept all types.
Map transforms each element, Filter selects, Reduce aggregates.
Pre-allocating with make avoids repeated append growth in Map.

Title: Worker Pool
Explain: Buffered channels decouple producers from consumers.
Workers range over jobCh and stop when it is closed.
WaitGroup ensures all workers finish before closing resCh.

Title: Select With Timeout
Explain: select multiplexes multiple channel operations.
Nested select prevents blocking on a full output channel.
Context cancellation provides graceful shutdown of all goroutines.

Title: Rate Limiter
Explain: Token bucket algorithm refills tokens based on elapsed time.
Mutex protects shared state from concurrent access.
Burst capacity allows short bursts above the steady rate.

Title: Concurrent Cache
Explain: RWMutex allows concurrent reads but exclusive writes.
TTL expiration is checked lazily on each Get call.
interface{} allows storing any value type in the cache.

Title: HTTP Middleware Chain
Explain: Middleware wraps handlers to add cross-cutting behavior.
Chain applies middlewares in reverse so the first listed runs first.
recover inside defer catches panics and returns a 500 response.

Title: Graceful Server Shutdown
Explain: signal.Notify captures OS signals for controlled shutdown.
select waits for either a server error or a shutdown signal.
Shutdown drains active connections within the timeout deadline.
ErrServerClosed is expected after Shutdown and is not a real error.

Title: Retry With Backoff
Explain: Exponential backoff increases delay between retries.
Jitter prevents thundering herd when many clients retry.
Context cancellation allows callers to abort the retry loop.
The last error is wrapped to preserve the failure chain.

Title: Concurrent Pipeline With Error Group
Explain: errgroup cancels sibling goroutines on first error.
Multiple parse workers fan out from a shared input channel.
Select on ctx.Done prevents goroutine leaks on cancellation.
Two-stage pipeline separates parsing from transformation.

Title: Circuit Breaker
Explain: Circuit breaker transitions through closed, open, and half-open states.
Open state fast-fails without calling the underlying function.
Half-open allows a single probe to test if the service recovered.
Mutex is released before calling fn to avoid holding locks during IO.
